$comment: Machine-readable record of how each upstream commit since the baseline was treated in this fork. docs/upstream-sync.md renders its Sync point section from this file; scripts/check-upstream-ports.mjs fails when the two drift, when a commit is unclassified, or when a decline rests on a host-capability claim the host contradicts.

upstreamRef.note: Full sha is re-derived by the check from the remote ref; recorded here for humans.

entries.reason: Long sessions accumulated inline images until every turn and compaction failed HTTP 413. The host executor that performs the offload ships in dsh-base on every version in our window; the plugin only asks, never trims history itself.

entries.subject: fix: support DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 and harden provider routing
entries.reason: Split, not cherry-picked. Ported: SSE readers now cancel the unread body, and signed replay is scoped to the originating account and model. Not ported: lockfile and devDependency floor moves, prepared-call routing, abort hardening, and release mechanics, which belong to a release strategy this fork does not use. Legacy unwrapped replay still passes through when provider and model match the route; that limit is stated in the code and the report rather than papered over.

entries.subject: test: tolerate the hourly refresh landing a few minutes past the hour
entries.reason: Hardens the schedule assertion belonging to f359301e: each run is scheduled an hour after the previous one finishes, and that run does file I/O a fixed settle budget cannot bound. This fork has not taken the hourly refresh — f359301e stays open below — so it has no schedule to harden.

entries.subject: chore: release v0.9.9
entries.reason: Upstream release line; the fork versions independently (see docs/compatibility.md).

entries.subject: fix(catalog-store): retry rename on Windows share-mode errors and cover concurrent saves (#129)
entries.reason: Split, not cherry-picked. The concurrent-save half was already covered here: 3987969 serializes catalog mutations per path and test/catalog-store.spec.ts proves overlapping account saves cannot drop a sibling snapshot, so upstream's regression test is not ported. The bounded rename retry on EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES is, with one deviation: it runs on Windows only, because on POSIX those codes are real failures and retrying would delay surfacing them by about 300 ms.

entries.subject: fix(pool): report the real cause of an exhausted pool instead of a synthetic RATE_LIMIT (#139)
entries.reason: Split, and the fork's reporting half goes further than upstream: 7aee561 returns a lone non-quota member failure as that same error, keeping its code, status, and cause, and reports RATE_LIMIT only when every failure really is a quota or rate limit; 441ff75 keeps the pool's earliest scoped recovery on it. e75b7c6 ports the other two halves: the terminal exhaustion now reaches onWarn, so dsh.log records the exhaustion that ends a failover, and a forced usage refresh from Settings clears that account's pool cooldowns. Two user actions force a refresh, the Refresh button and the re-check that follows a reset-credit redemption attempt, whether or not the redemption succeeded; no background poll does. The cooldown clears even when the re-check itself fails.

entries.subject: feat(settings): choose the Claude prompt-cache TTL from the manage dialog
entries.reason: e3fcd52 ported the config-level TTL; 9045486 adds the Manage dialog's Prompt cache lifetime picker on this fork's rewritten dialog. The choice is a Claude-only provider preference, promptCacheTtl, not a per-account one; the adapter re-reads it on every request, so a save applies from the next turn, and compaction and session-title requests stay at five minutes. 733c682 makes a models-only Save take the TTL from the freshly re-read settings instead of writing back the value the model editor loaded.

entries.reason: Reimplemented on the fork's editor using the 6ea68cb final tree. Saved visibility and subagent-speed ids remain rows; account-neutral Cursor keeps generic empty-catalog copy.
